payload.name: CaptureIdiomaticCommitmentExpressions
payload.description: When a message conveys a speaker's resolve or refusal using idioms like 'not giving up' or 'won't stop', during extraction capture the underlying commitment as a memory.
content: During extraction, map idiomatic or indirect expressions of a speaker's resolve, refusal, or commitment (e.g., 'I'm not giving up', 'I won't stop', 'no quitting') to the concrete action they imply, and create a candidate memory for the speaker (type state or plan) that records the commitment or avoidance.
Do not extract when the statement is non-committal, hypothetical, or refers to someone else.

solves: The extraction stage missed a memory when a speaker used an idiomatic refusal ('I'm not giving up') instead of a literal statement ('I will not quit'). The mechanism is an over-literal parse that fails to resolve common idioms to their concrete action. This skill applies to any future message in which a speaker indirectly expresses commitment or avoidance; it does not cover hypothetical or third-party statements.
